serviceNotes: A2L (mildly flammable): ventilate the work area, no ignition sources or open flame nearby, use an A2L-rated leak detector and A2L-rated recovery machine, cylinders have left-hand-thread valves, purge with dry nitrogen before brazing, never retrofit A1 equipment to an A2L refrigerant.

NEVER charge R-454B into R-410A equipment, and never top off an R-454B system with R-410A: it is not a drop-in, the equipment listing (UL 60335-2-40) and the refrigerant detection system (RDS) mitigation are specific to A2L.
Near-azeotropic (≈ 2.7 °F glide at 40 °F): charge as liquid; use dew point for superheat and bubble point for subcooling.
Pressures ≈ 5 % below R-410A (113 psig bubble at 40 °F vs 119). R-410A gauges and hoses are pressure-rated, but the detector and recovery machine must be A2L-rated; cylinders are left-hand thread.
Equipment with an RDS: on a leak alarm the unit runs the blower and disables the compressor/ignition — check the RDS fault before refrigerant work.
Table values above 133 °F are extrapolated with a Clausius–Clapeyron fit (CoolProp mixture flash failed above that temperature); treat high-side readings above 133 °F saturation as approximate.

lubricant: MO or PAO (immiscible; oil separation/draining required)
applications: Industrial refrigeration (cold storage, food processing, ice rinks)
serviceNotes: B2L — HIGHER TOXICITY and mildly flammable. Odor threshold ~5 ppm; IDLH 300 ppm. Wear a full-face respirator with ammonia cartridge (SCBA for releases), gloves and eye protection; know the emergency shutoff and eyewash locations; follow the site's PSM/RMP procedures where the charge is > 10,000 lb.
Ammonia attacks copper and brass: steel/stainless piping only; oil is immiscible and must be drained from oil pots (purge/drain with the valve procedure, never crack a plugged drain open).
Trace water raises the boiling point; air/non-condensables collect in the condenser (purger).
Typical 40 °F ≈ 59 psig; 100 °F ≈ 197 psig; suction goes into vacuum below −28 °F.

applications: Supermarket transcritical booster racks and cascade low stages
serviceNotes: Critical temperature 87.8 °F (31 °C): above that there is no saturation — the system runs TRANSCRITICAL (gas cooler, not condenser) and high-side pressure is controlled, not a function of temperature. Table stops at 86 °F.

Very high pressures: 553 psig at 40 °F, ~955 psig at 80 °F, transcritical high side 1,200–1,600 psig. Use CO2-rated gauges/hoses/components; standby PRVs lift near 500–650 psig on the low side when power is lost.
Never isolate liquid CO2 between closed valves (hydrostatic burst). Vapor charge to above the triple point (60.4 psig / −69.8 °F) before adding liquid, or dry ice forms and blocks lines.
A1 but an asphyxiant: monitor with a CO2 detector in machine rooms (alarm 5,000 ppm typical).
